solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Film invalid — delete freely (4,3,3,3)

indicatorNotes.freely: the letters are to be arranged freely, in any order

annotation.surface: A curt editorial note telling someone to cut a worthless film without restraint.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'delete freely' look like an instruction to an editor; in fact both words before it are raw letters for the Bond film title.
annotation.definitionFit: A title: the 1973 James Bond film, Roger Moore's first as 007, takes its name from the Paul McCartney theme song.

entries.clue: Noble queen left with earl hosted by loquacious heroine (4,10)

indicatorNotes.hosted by: a host takes guests in, so the talkative word takes the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.with: 'with' means accompanied by, so earl travels alongside queen and left into the same host

blocks.note: chatty = talkative; it hosts the next three pieces
E = earl, as in peerage lists

annotation.surface: A gossipy heroine entertains a titled queen and an earl.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Noble' looks like the definition, but it supplies only the first word; the heroine is the definition, and 'hosted by' makes the talkative word wrap the royal and peerage abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: Lady Chatterley is the heroine of D. H. Lawrence's novel Lady Chatterley's Lover.

entries.clue: Large fiddle comprises half of offences (5)

indicatorNotes.half of: keep only the first half of the word

blocks.note: offences = VIOLATIONS, ten letters; keep the first five

annotation.surface: A big violin somehow makes up half of the crimes on record.
annotation.walkthrough: You must find the ten-letter synonym for offences before you can halve it.
annotation.definitionFit: The viola is a slightly larger member of the violin family.

entries.clue: Symbolic storyteller building toy trails around houses (10)

indicatorNotes.around: the letters of TRAILS are moved around

blocks.note: Lego is the plastic building toy

annotation.surface: A storyteller of symbolic tales traces paths around the houses in a toy town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Building toy' reads as a toy being built, but it is a single noun for the toy, which the shuffled trails then house.
annotation.definitionFit: An allegorist writes allegories, stories whose characters and events stand for something else.

entries.clue: Tried to get connection put up on type of display? (7)

indicatorNotes.put up: in a down clue, 'up' turns LAID over
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, DIAL sits on top of LED

annotation.surface: Someone tries to hook up a connection to some kind of screen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put up' is one instruction: LAID written upwards. The question mark flags that LED is only one type of display.
annotation.definitionFit: To dial a number is to try to get a telephone connection.

entries.clue: Intensify limit of humanitarian assistance, mainly in European church (7)

indicatorNotes.limit of: the end letter of the word
indicatorNotes.mainly: most of the word, so drop its last letter

blocks.note: HAND (assistance, as in 'give a hand') without its last letter

annotation.surface: A call to step up aid efforts inside a European church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Humanitarian assistance' reads as one aid-agency phrase, but it splits into two separate pieces, and 'European church' likewise wraps around the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to enhance a flavour or effect is to heighten or intensify it.

entries.clue: Mysterious closure of blood vessel (4)

indicatorNotes.closure of: the letter that closes the word, its last

annotation.surface: A strange blockage in a blood vessel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blood vessel' is one medical phrase, but it splits in two: 'vessel' is a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: Dark means hidden or obscure, as in dark secrets.

entries.clue: Found 10 packed in box south of river (9)

indicatorNotes.south of: in a down clue, CRATED goes below EXE

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

annotation.surface: Something is found packed in a box downstream of a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 10 across is ABHORRENT, so the definition reads 'found abhorrent'. 'Found' looks like 'discovered', but here it means 'judged'.
annotation.definitionFit: To execrate something is to find it abhorrent and denounce it.

entries.clue: What might be seen as positive symbol for part of the UK (2,7,5)

annotation.definition: What might be seen as positive symbol for part of the UK

blocks.note: the surface pushes an upbeat emblem; the setter means the plus sign, +, as marked on a battery
England, whose flag is a red upright cross on white, shaped like +

annotation.surface: An upbeat emblem representing one of the home nations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Positive' seems to mean upbeat, but the positive symbol is +. England's flag has exactly that shape. St Andrew's Cross (Scotland) is an X, not a +.
annotation.definitionFit: St George's Cross is the flag of England, a red plus-shaped cross on white.

entries.clue: Amusing pretty girl runs boards (5)

indicatorNotes.boards: to board is to take someone in as a lodger, so DOLL takes R in

blocks.note: a doll is dated slang for a pretty girl

annotation.surface: An entertaining pretty girl manages a boarding house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runs boards' sounds like managing a lodging house; here 'boards' means takes in as a lodger.
annotation.definitionFit: Droll means amusing in a dry or odd way.

entries.clue: Obscene rating split half of “horsey” bores (9)

indicatorNotes.split: the gap between AB and RENT is opened up
indicatorNotes.half of: keep the first half of the word
indicatorNotes.bores: HOR bores its way into the gap

blocks.note: AB = able seaman, a naval rating
first three of HORSEY's six letters

annotation.surface: A rude remark about horsey people being dull.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bores' looks like a noun for dull people; it is a verb, drilling the half-word into the gap between the other two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means repugnant or offensive, close to obscene in its sense of 'disgusting'.

entries.clue: Finally suing after Guardian feature covers substituted child (10)

indicatorNotes.Finally: the last letter of the next word
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means following, so the last letter of suing is placed following the rest
indicatorNotes.covers: to cover something is to go over and around it, so the feature wraps round the guardian

blocks.note: a facial feature; it covers ANGEL

annotation.surface: A newspaper feature ends with a lawsuit over a swapped child.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital G makes 'Guardian' look like the newspaper; it is a guardian angel.
annotation.definitionFit: In folklore a changeling is a fairy child secretly swapped for a human baby.

entries.clue: Lavish with compliments? (4)

blocks.note: 'with compliments' is printed on things given at no charge

annotation.surface: Someone is heaping on the praise.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about flattery, but 'with compliments' is the phrase on a free gift, and being free with money means being lavish.
annotation.definitionFit: Free means both generous and complimentary, without charge.

entries.clue: Lawmaker on trial — so unexpected (10)

indicatorNotes.unexpected: the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

annotation.surface: A politician finds themselves on trial, to everyone's surprise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link word, but it gives LEG: in cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field.
annotation.definitionFit: A legislator is a member of a law-making body.

entries.clue: Guaranteed return of some comrade Russians one’s abandoned (7)

indicatorNotes.some: take only some of the letters
indicatorNotes.abandoned: to abandon is to leave behind, so one (I) is left out of the letters

blocks.note: the run of letters inside comraDE RUSSIAns

annotation.surface: A promise that some Russian comrades will return, though one has defected.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters are hidden across 'comrade Russians', then one I is dropped and the rest read backwards. A letter taken out of a hidden word is rare.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an assured result is one that is guaranteed, certain to happen.

entries.clue: Instrument captured spirit (5,4)

annotation.surface: A tool that trapped a ghost.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a ghost to go with 'captured', but it is a drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument with wires stretched across its underside.

entries.clue: Horse trainers encourage racing primarily on flat (7)

indicatorNotes.primarily: take the first letter of each word
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, TER goes after EVEN

blocks.note: first letters of trainers, encourage, racing

annotation.surface: Horse trainers promote racing on the flat, not over jumps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Racing on the flat' is real racing language, so 'flat' seems to belong to the sport; it just gives EVEN.
annotation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse trained for eventing, which combines dressage, cross-country and show jumping.

entries.clue: Essentially potty release price for component of Windows (7)

indicatorNotes.Essentially: the essence, or central letter, of the word

blocks.note: a ransom is the price paid for a captive's release

annotation.surface: A mad demand to pay for part of Microsoft's operating system.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital W makes it look like the software; a transom is a crossbar in a real window.
annotation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal bar across a window or above a door.

entries.clue: Piece about island inhabited by unknown poet (7)

indicatorNotes.inhabited by: Z lives inside the other pieces

blocks.note: a chess or draughts piece is a man
x, y and z are the algebra unknowns
on = about, as in a talk on a subject

annotation.surface: An article about an island where an obscure poet lives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unknown poet' reads as one phrase, but 'unknown' only gives the algebra letter, which inhabits the string built from piece, about and island.
annotation.definitionFit: Alessandro Manzoni was an Italian poet and novelist, author of I promessi sposi.

entries.clue: Adult regularly wearing pig skin (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken

blocks.note: a swine is a pig; it goes around DL

annotation.surface: A grown-up routinely dressed in pigskin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pig skin' looks like leather, but 'skin' is the definition, a verb meaning to fleece someone.
annotation.definitionFit: To skin someone is slang for cheating them out of money, as a swindle does.

entries.clue: Way to classify alien (7)

blocks.note: to range things is to arrange or class them

annotation.surface: A method for categorising extraterrestrials.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alien' seems to be a noun needing classification; it is the adjective, meaning foreign or unfamiliar.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something alien is foreign and unfamiliar, and so strange to you.

entries.clue: Smell ultimate in fear that’s terrifying (4)

indicatorNotes.ultimate in: the last letter of the word

blocks.note: 'eek!' is what you say at something terrifying

annotation.surface: A smell so bad it frightens people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That's terrifying' is the reaction itself: the cry EEK.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as noun or verb: to give off a strong, usually foul, odour.

entries.clue: Barren crop in mostly fluid ground (10)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word but not all, so its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.ground: the letters are ground up and remixed

annotation.surface: A failed harvest on waterlogged land.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like soil for the crop, but it means crushed: the letters are remixed.
annotation.definitionFit: Barren land is unproductive, not prolific.

entries.clue: Makes more stable companies (5)

blocks.note: to firm (up) is to make firmer

annotation.surface: Companies strengthen their position.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence, subject after verb; it is really two separate definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Firms is both a verb (makes firm) and a plural noun (businesses).

entries.clue: Sound spanned by Port Hudson (4)

indicatorNotes.spanned by: the answer is bridged across the two words

annotation.surface: A strait or bridge crossing between two places named Port and Hudson.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a stretch of water to match the port and river; it is a noise.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a thud is one particular sound, the dull noise of something heavy landing.

entries.clue: Human attention beginning to be engaged by old character (9)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the first letter of the next word
indicatorNotes.engaged by: to be engaged by is to be taken on and held, so the old letter holds B inside it

blocks.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
thorn (þ) is an Old English letter for 'th'; it takes in B

annotation.surface: An ancient figure catches a person's attention as it begins to arrive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old character' means an old letter, not a person: thorn. EAR + TH(B)ORN.
annotation.definitionFit: Earthborn means born on earth, and so human or mortal.

entries.clue: Trunk’s more or less on time (5)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, OR SO goes after T

blocks.note: 'or so' = approximately, as in 'ten or so'

annotation.surface: A travel trunk that arrives roughly on schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests luggage or an elephant, but it is the body's trunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Your trunk is the main part of your body, the torso.

entries.clue: Stressful period, arguably, if credit is doubled (3-4,6)

indicatorNotes.doubled: doubled means made twice as many, so IS appears two times

blocks.note: IF is in the middle of lIFe, so it is 'mid-life', arguably

annotation.surface: Doubling your credit could be a stressful time.
annotation.walkthrough: The playful step: IF sits in the middle of LIFE, so 'if' can be called MID-LIFE, and 'arguably' admits the stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: A midlife crisis is the anxious period some people go through in middle age.
